title: When and Why Consumers “Accidentally” Endanger Their Products
authors: Yaniv Shani; Gil Appel; Shai Danziger; Ron Shachar
main_or_robustness: Study 1a only (field data); other studies are experiments

ineligible_specs.exclusion_reason: 2x2 DiD on two aggregate daily time series (damaged vs used iPhone 4 listings) around one product-launch date per analysis; Weekend and Weekend x Damaged regressors; no unit panel, no staggered adoption

eligible_reason: Not staggered. Study 1a regresses standardized daily listing counts for two series (damaged vs used iPhone 4) on Damaged, Event, Damaged x Event, Weekend and Weekend x Damaged in a 28- or 14-day window around a single launch (white iPhone 4 in April 2011; iPhone 4S announcement/launch in October 2011), N = 112 series-days. Each analysis has one event date and two 'units'. Studies 1b, 1c, 2, 3a, 3b are online experiments.
design_notes: Published text Section 'Study 1a: Damaged Products', equation in Meyer (1995) spirit. The package contains no code.
data_files_note: Only experiment data (Studies 1B, 1C, 2, 3A, 3B) as xlsx plus a one-line readme; the scraped listing data for Study 1a and all code are not shipped.
data_provenance_note: Field data for the only DiD analysis (Study 1a) not shipped; experiment data are original.
screener_notes: Published PDF read (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2019.3509.txt). Empty regression inventory because no code is shipped.
